CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  August 9, 2021 - 4:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconferen ce/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the meeting to order at 4:34 p.m. The pledge
  of allegiance was led by Councilmember Madison.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
 Council members:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Councilmember Kennedy stated the following for the record:

  "Jayce Ward served the residents of Pasadena with honor,
  courage, and leadership for 37 years. Jayce began his career as a
  full time police officer in 1984 and was promoted to Corporal in
  1999. Jayce was reared in the City of Pasadena. He was a
  dedicated and a passionate peace officer in our City.

  Jayce worked many assignments within the Pasadena Police
  Department, including the Neighborhood Crime Task Force, School
  Resource Division, Robbery - Detective, Field Training Coordinator
  and Patrol. Officer Ward was responsible for starting the Pasadena
  Activities League (P.A.L.). The P.A.L. program was successful, in
  large measure, because of Jayce's emotional I.Q., life-experiences,
  leadership, and sheer tenacity. Jayce Ward earned the respect of
  his peers because of his mentoring of younger officers,
  professionalism and commitment to the residents of the city of
  Pasadena. Jayce Ward has received numerous commendations
  from his supervisors and community members acknowledging his
  contribution to crime fighting and much needed community-building
  efforts.

  Finally, as we celebrate Corporal Jayce Ward's 37 years of service
  to Pasadena, we encourage the wonderful diversity in Pasadena to
  apply to become a police officer with the Pasadena Police
  Department. Where else can you earn over $300,000 in public
  service, when you include overtime pay?

Council Minutes  1  08/09/2021
   Again, Corporal Jayce Ward, thank you for 37 years of exemplary
  service to Pasadena. We wish you well in all of your future
  endeavors."

  Mayor Gordo on behalf of the City Council thanked Corporal Ward
  for his exemplary service to the City.

  Corporal Jayce Ward expressed his appreciation and thanked the
  City Council, including Councilmember Kennedy, for the recognition
  on his years of service to the community.

PUBLIC COMMENT  Sonja Berndt, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns on the
  limited time for the public to review and analyze the staffs
  recommendations related to the City's American Rescue Plan Act
  funds and advocated for those funds to be used towards affordable
  housing and housing insecurities.

  The  following  individuals  expressed  concerns  with
  Councilmembers who turn off their Zoom video cameras during
  public comment, advocated for the termination of Pasadena Police
  Chief Perez, Officers Dumaguindin, Serrano, and Mulrooney, and
  City Manager Steve Mermell; and/or spoke on controversial
  incidents involving Pasadena police officers.

  Jasmine Richards Abdullah, representing  Black  Lives
  Pasadena
  Adriana Bautista, Pasadena resident

PUBLIC HEARING  PUBLIC HEARING: PROPOSED ZONING CODE
  AMENDMENTS TO THE CITY'S CANNABIS REGULATIONS
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  ( 1) Find that the actions proposed in the agenda report are exempt
  from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption);
  and 15301 (Existing Facilities); there are no features that distinguish
  this action from others in the exempt class, and there are no unique
  circumstances; and
  (2) Direct the City Attorney's Office to prepare an ordinance to
  amend the Zoning Code to adopt the proposed Cannabis
  Regulations with the findings contained in Attachment A of the
  agenda report, as follows:

Council Minutes  7  08/09/2021
   1. Allow up to three cannabis retailers per council district instead of
  one;and
  2. Decrease the required distance between cannabis retailers from
  1,000 feet to 450 feet.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, opened the public hearing; reported that
  the public hearing notice was published in the Pasadena Press on
  July 26, July 29, 2021, and August 5, 2021; 8 letters/emails in
  support of the staff recommendation and providing comment, 3
  letters/emails in opposition to the staff recommendation, and
  providing comment, and 1 letter expressing concerns with one of
  the City's licensed cannabis retailers were received by the City
  Clerk's Office, which were distributed to the City Council, posted on-
  line, and made part of the public record.

  City Manager Mermell provided a historical oral overview of the
  City's cannabis retailer process, and David Reyes, Director of
  Planning and Community Development, presented a PowerPoint
  presentation on the item, and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Hampton, Chair of the Economic Development and
  Technology Committee, summarized the Committee's discussion
  and recommendation on the matter, and responded to questions

  Councilmember Kennedy expressed strong concerns with the staff
  recommendation, describing the work as "shoddy," resulting in the
  possibility of three cannabis retailers operating in City Council
  District 3, which he also believes to be discriminatory; and with the
  cannabis license permitting process. He also expressed concerns
  with a cannabis retailer that was provided a license, which was sold
  to a different corporation. Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the
  need for staff and the City Council to address the California
  Cannabis Equity Act of 2018 prior to moving forward with the staff
  recommendation. In addition, he requested that staff number the
  PowerPoint presentation slides so that the Councilmembers may
  refer to slides efficiently once the presentation is complete.

  Theresa Fuentes, Assistant City Attorney, provided information on
  the City's Change of Control and Change of Ownership rubric that
  is utilized prior to an issuance of a cannabis permit; and responded
  to questions.

  Councilmember Williams asked staff to provide information on
  Harvest of Pasadena change of control prior to February 2021.

  Mayor Gordo requested that staff to analyze State legislation
  related to Conditional Use Permits and cannabis retailers.

  Councilmember  Masuda  echoed  concerns  raised  by
  Councilmember Kennedy, and spoke in opposition to the staff

Council Minutes  8  08/09/2021
   recommendation that would allow more than one cannabis retailer
  per City Council District.

  The following individuals provide comments and suggestions on the
  matter:

  Douglas Smurr, representing Harvest of Pasadena, LLC
  Pattyl Aposhian, Pasadena resident
  Dave Barmore, representing MedMen
  Wesley Tyner, Pasadena resident
  Tim Dodd, representing Sweet Flower Pasadena, LLC

  Councilmember Kennedy expressed strong concerns with the over
  concentration of cannabis retailers in Council District 3, and staff's
  recommendation as presented to the City Council; and advocated
  for cannabis retailers to be permitted throughout the City (rather
  than concentrated in one Council District) and that the social equity
  component be designed in such a way as to benefit those
  communities and individuals that have been discriminated against
  in prior enforcement of cannabis laws.

  Vice Mayor Wilson spoke on the City's cannabis regulatory scheme
  that was set in motion which is to follow through on the City's voters
  request to have a number of cannabis retailers in the City. He spoke
  in favor of the staff recommendation, and on the need for a Social
  Equity component related to the City's cannabis retailers.

  Councilmember Madison echoed Vice Mayor Wilson's comments.

  Motion:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Hampton,
  seconded by Councilmember Rivas, to close the public hearing:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Madison, Masuda, Rivas,
  Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor Gordo
  NOES:  Councilmember Kennedy
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  Councilmember Rivas summarized the discussion at the Economic
  Development and Technology (EDTech) Committee regarding
  directing staff to return to the Committee with a recommendation on
  a City Social Equity component and advocated to direct staff to
  return with such a recommendation in eight months to the City
  Council.

  Councilmember Williams expressed concerns with staff report that
  lacks an evaluation of the staff recommendations or options; and
  the changing of the cannabis permit process rules mid-stream. She
  spoke on the need for the City Council to determine the City's land
  uses taking into consideration the needs of the residents, and not

Council Minutes  9  08/09/2021
   private entities; and advocated for a thoughtful cannabis permitting
  process that includes social equity. Councilmember Williams spoke
  in favor of allowing the current cannabis retailers Conditional Use
  Permits to expire, and start over with another round of applications
  that includes a social equity program.

  Mayor Gordo spoke on the staff and EDTech Committee discussion
  and recommendation, and spoke in favor of the staff
  recommendation, which he believes meets the voter's intent in
  relation to the City's regulations, ensures reasonable safeguards
  and distance requirements in place to protect neighborhoods and
  sensitive uses. He spoke on the need for the EDTech Committee to
  define "social equity" and determine any impacts in terms of
  changes to the cannabis ordinance.

  Councilmember Kennedy recommended that staff use SB 1294 -
  The California Cannabis Equity Act as a guide on social equity; and
  advocated that this item be held until the City's 2021 redistricting
  process is complete.

  Following further discussion, it was moved by Councilmember
  Hampton, seconded by Vice Mayor Wilson, to approve the staff
  recommendation, including direction to staff to provide a
  recommendation within eight months on a social equity program at
  a future City Council meeting:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Madison, Rivas, Vice
  Mayor Wilson, Mayor Gordo
  NOES:  Councilmembers Kennedy, Masuda, Williams

  ABSTAIN: None
